data.name: Holofernes
data.gender_notes: Holofernes is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In the Old Testament Book of Judith, Holofernes is the Assyrian military commander leading an invasion of Judah. After being tricked by the widow Judith, he is killed, paving the way for Jewish victory. The name Holofernes carries the meaning “Captain of the Assyrian army” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Holofernes usually hope their child will grow to embody captain of the assyrian army and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes courage and faith in the face of adversity
data.etymology: Holofernes belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Captain of the Assyrian army.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Holofernes total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.
data.cultural_impact: Holofernes is remembered in history as a symbol of Babylonian power and military might, whose downfall ultimately represented the triumph of the Jewish people and their faith.
data.spiritual_significance: St. Holofernes was later canonized as a martyr in the Roman Catholic Church. His death, resulting from a cunning manifestation of faith, serves as an inspiration to those facing overwhelming adversity and a call to trust in the power of God.
